raw_response:
I'm a 44-year-old farmer in Quzhou County, Hebei. I've been farming for 25 years — my father taught me, and now I manage this land myself. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension leaflets when they come around, but honestly most of what I know comes from watching my own fields and talking to my neighbors over tea.

I've got 10.1 mu, all in wheat-maize double cropping. That's the only system that makes sense here — the land doesn't sit idle. My household has seven people, but my wife and I are the main ones on the farm. My son and his wife work in Shijiazhuang and send some money home, which helps, but I still watch every yuan. I can't afford to waste inputs, and I can't afford a bad year either.

**Wheat this year:** I'll plant around October 10th, same as always. I buy improved wheat seed — about 60 yuan per mu. I used to save my own seed, but the yield dropped after a few years, so now I buy fresh. For fertilizer, the extension guy says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I usually do a bit more because I'd rather waste a little money than see my wheat turn yellow at jointing. I'll put down about 25 kg per mu of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base at sowing — that gives me some phosphorus and potassium too — and then topdress about 25 kg per mu of urea at green-up in March. That works out to roughly 16 kg N per mu total. I irrigate three times: winter water in late November, jointing water in late March, and one more at grain filling in May. Water costs about 50 yuan per mu for the season, but without it the yield crashes. For pesticides, I'll spray herbicide once after sowing and an insecticide for aphids in spring — about 40 yuan per mu. Tillage is rotary tillage before planting, 50 yuan per mu. My wife and I do most of the work, but at harvest in early June I might hire one or two people for a couple of days if the weather window is tight. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Maize this year:** The hard part is always the turnaround. We harvest wheat in early June, and within a week I need maize in the ground. I'll plant around June 12th. I buy hybrid maize seed every year — never save it — about 55 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put down compound at planting, about 20 kg per mu, and then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage in July, about 20 kg per mu. That's about 12 kg N per mu total. Maize needs less fuss than wheat. I irrigate twice — once at jointing and once at filling if July and August are dry. Another 50 yuan per mu. Herbicide once at planting, maybe one insecticide if the borers show up — about 30 yuan per mu. Tillage is quick rotary tillage right after wheat harvest, 50 yuan per mu. Harvest is in late September, and maize harvest is more work than wheat — I usually hire help for a couple of days. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

**Why I'm doing it this way:** Last year was decent — I got about 1000 jin per mu of wheat and 1100 jin of maize. I'm not changing much because change is risky. My neighbor tried cutting fertilizer last year to save money and his wheat looked terrible in April. I learned from that. We have some off-farm income, so I don't have to under-apply inputs out of desperation, but I also don't experiment. I know what works, I know what it costs, and I stick to it. The biggest worry is always water — the wells are metered now and electricity isn't cheap. Three times for wheat, two for maize. That's what I can afford, and it's usually enough.
